I will keep the full 16.9 mu in my usual wheat-maize rotation, because I know this system well, I have 35 years of experience with it, and my well irrigation lets me hold yield more steadily than relying only on rainfall. Since my household is small and some labor is off-farm, I will keep management practical and not overly complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the fertilizer into nitrogen with a solid phosphorus base, add some potassium, irrigate a few key times, and protect the crop with a limited number of pesticide sprays so I do not let disease or weeds cut yield. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield and stability, keep fertilizer moderate but adequate, irrigate when summer rainfall is not enough, and use a few pesticide applications to control weeds and pests. I will rely on rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and fits the wheat-maize rotation well. My goal is steady production with manageable labor and input use, not taking unnecessary risk.
